newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM forms leftist coalition government.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM forms leftist coalition government.

text.p: Slovenia's prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek said on Friday, after weeks of deadlock following an inconclusive general election, that he had formed a leftist government with a slender majority.
"Some minutes ago my government proposal was agreed by the highest body of my party and I will hand it to the president of parliament in an hour," Drnovsek told a news conference.
Talks with three rightist parties had failed earlier in the day.

Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats will form a coalition with former communist party the United List of Social Democrats, the Desus party which represents pensioners and the Nationalist Party. The government also has the support of three independent deputies, giving it 46 votes.
"I tried all possibilities to achieve a large and strong government," Drnovsek said.

Marjan Podobnik, leader of the conservative People's Party, said earlier the differences between the Liberal Democrats and an alliance of three rightist parties were too great and no agreement for a coalition could be found.
Drnovsek had held intensive talks for 15 days to form a government after weeks of political deadlock which followed an inconclusive general election on November 10.
But he failed to win over the rightist "Spring" alliance, comprising the People's Party, the centre-right Social Democrats and the Christian Democrats, that hold 44 out of 90 parliamentary seats.
"Because of the existing two blocs in parliament...it was impossible to find an intermediate government," Drnovsek said.
He said efforts would continue to form a broader coalition.
"It is in my interest that we reach a larger coalition and I am open to discussion on that in the hope that there may be a possibility of reconstructing the government in the future," Drnovsek said.

According to the proposed agreement the Liberal Democrats will get nine ministerial posts and the United List five, while Desus and the Nationalist Party will each have one seat in the new government.

The Liberal Democrats will provide the foreign minister, the finance minister and the minister for economic affairs. Drnovsek said the finance and economic ministers in the acting government would stay on in their posts.

The new foreign minister will be Zoran Thaler, who held the same post for over a year until May 1996 when he was ousted by parliament, accused of blocking progress in Slovenia's association agreement with the European Union.
Drnovsek has not yet named candidates for the ministries of agriculture and justice and said he would name them next week.
Parliamentary bodies have to approve ministerial candidates within seven days, after which the vote in parliament is taken.
Earlier in the day, Social Democrat leader Janez Jansa said Drnovsek faced problems ahead.
"A government with a minimal majority can make some decisions but not key strategic decisions," Jansa, a former defence minister, told state radio.
One stumbling block could be changes to the constitution to enable Slovenia to join the EU -- a parliamentary vote which would need a two-thirds majority.
The new government will be Slovenia's third since independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991. Drnovsek has been acting prime minister since April 1992.
